svg.title: GI bleeding decision chart: resuscitate and correct coagulopathy first, then sort by the ligament of Treitz; an upper bleed is non-variceal (IV pantoprazole and endoscopic therapy) or variceal (pantoprazole, octreotide, antibiotics, banding), a lower bleed goes to colonoscopy if stable or to upper endoscopy, angiography and surgery if unstable

svg.text: GI bleed: RESUSCITATE first, then UPPER or LOWER (the ligament of Treitz)?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: airway (intubate if needed) · 2 large-bore IVs · fluids · transfuse

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: correct coagulopathy: fresh frozen plasma, platelets, vitamin K, Octaplex · STOP anticoagulants and antiplatelets

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: NO visible blood (OCCULT: positive fecal occult blood or iron deficiency anemia) → rule out colorectal and other cancers
